note: Countries that adopted sanctions against Russia after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022, status October 2026, compiled by Orbis from official sources. EU: the 27 member states apply EU sanctions decided unanimously by the Council (Council of the EU, 'EU sanctions against Russia explained', https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/sanctions-against-russia-explained/, last review 7 October 2026). Aligned with EU sanctions: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Norway (plus Ukraine) 'align themselves' with EU Council Decision (CFSP) 2025/931 (High Representative statement, 4 June 2025, https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2025/06/04/statement-by-the-high-representative-on-behalf-of-the-eu-on-the-alignment-of-certain-countries-concerning-restrictive-measures-in-view-of-russia-s-actions-destabilising-the-situation-in-ukraine/); Switzerland: Federal Council adopted the EU packages on 28 February 2022 (https://www.admin.ch/gov/en/start/documentation/media-releases.msg-id-87386.html); Monaco applies EU asset freezes by ministerial decision (https://geldefonds.gouv.mc); San Marino: Decree-Law No. 35 of 15 March 2022 and later decrees adopting EU measures (Consiglio Grande e Generale); Andorra adopts EU packages by government decree (reported by Altaveu, May 2026); Kosovo: government decision 01/64 of 25 February 2022 and later amendments aligning with EU and US measures (reported by Prishtina Insight and Kossev; no official English text found). Own sanctions: United States (OFAC, https://ofac.treasury.gov/sanctions-programs-and-country-information/russian-harmful-foreign-activities-sanctions); United Kingdom (https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/uk-sanctions-on-russia); Canada (https://www.international.gc.ca/world-monde/international_relations-relations_internationales/sanctions/russia-russie.aspx); Japan (statement by Prime Minister Kishida, 25 February 2022, measures under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act); South Korea (export controls and financial measures announced from 24 and 28 February 2022, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy); Australia (DFAT, Russia sanctions regime, https://www.dfat.gov.au/international-relations/security/sanctions/sanctions-regimes/russia-sanctions-regime); New Zealand (Russia Sanctions Act 2022, https://www.mfat.govt.nz/en/countries-and-regions/europe/ukraine/russian-invasion-of-ukraine/sanctions); Singapore (MFA, 5 March 2022, https://www.mfa.gov.sg/Newsroom/Press-Statements-Transcripts-and-Photos/2022/03/20220305-sanctions); Taiwan (MOFA press release No. 038, 25 February 2022, https://en.mofa.gov.tw/News_Content.aspx?n=1328&s=97420, and MOEA export control lists); Ukraine (National Security and Defense Council sanctions; also aligns with EU decisions). Not shown: measures limited to individual listings or to other sanctions regimes (for example Moldova aligns with some EU listings, but not with the June 2025 decision); countries that only restricted their airspace or ended specific deals.
